result.title: Robust Function Calling for LLM Agents Under Interface Drift
result.comment: 16 pages, 1 figure, 6 tables. Peer-reviewed and accepted at NGEN-AI 2026 (International Conference on Next Generation AI Systems). This is the pre-review submitted version
result.summary: Tool-augmented language-model agents rely on interface text: tool descriptions, argument schemas, and the candidate tool list shown at inference time. These interfaces often change after deployment even when the underlying tool semantics remain fixed, creating a practical reliability problem for function-calling systems. We study this failure mode as interface drift and evaluate whether a lightweight, training-free repair layer can recover robustness without retraining the base model. Our method, SchemaShield-Lite, combines schema validation, candidate-set retry for missing tool names, and one-shot constrained repair. On Qwen3.5-9B, it raises DICE-300 accuracy from 0.717 to 0.813 and BFCL-200 accuracy from 0.580 to 0.805, recovering 19/22 and 33/45 drift-induced failures with no observed repair harms. Naive retry does not explain the gains. Ablations show that candidate-set drift, especially distractor tools, accounts for most observed damage, while description and schema edits alone are less harmful. The results position validation-and-repair as a practical robustness layer for deployed LLM-agent tool use.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究工具增强 LLM agent 在「接口漂移」（工具描述、参数 schema、候选工具列表变更）下的函数调用可靠性，提出免训练的校验与一次性约束修复层 SchemaShield-Lite，并在 DICE-300 与 BFCL-200 上报告错误恢复效果。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究问题是文本工具接口漂移下的调用鲁棒性与 schema 层工程修补，不涉及视觉或多模态推理状态、latent 生成、视觉证据筛选或停止决策，其候选集重试与修复机制也未给出可核查地向 LVR 迁移的具体线索，故排除。
